title: A Review of Generative AI in Computer Science Education: Challenges and Opportunities in Accuracy, Authenticity, and Assessment
extended_summary:
This paper reviews recent literature on generative AI use in computer science education, focusing on three interrelated concerns: accuracy, authenticity, and assessment. The authors ask how tools such as ChatGPT, Claude, and AI-assisted code generation affect teaching and learning, especially when AI outputs may be incorrect, biased, or difficult to distinguish from student-authored work.

Rather than reporting a new experiment, the paper synthesizes 52 studies published from 2019 to 2024 from sources including IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, and SpringerLink. The review covers how GenAI is used for code generation, troubleshooting, feedback, grading, and formative/summative assessment in computer science education, with emphasis on the risks of hallucinations, error propagation, bias, academic integrity concerns, and the limitations of AI-only evaluation.

The paper concludes that generative AI can improve efficiency, provide immediate feedback, and support creativity, but it should not replace human judgment. The authors argue for hybrid AI-human assessment models, stronger AI literacy for students and educators, bias detection and mitigation frameworks, and clearer policies around responsible AI use. They also identify the need for more long-term, empirical research on how inaccuracies, AI-generated feedback, and AI-supported assessment affect learning outcomes over time.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a narrative literature review/survey, not a primary empirical study, experiment, or meta-analysis. It provides no original causal design or quantitative synthesis sufficient for higher evidence grading.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper highlights important and broad implications for AI use in education, but it does not estimate direct effects in K-12 or general populations. Its impact is therefore conceptual and policy-relevant rather than empirically demonstrated.

interventions.use_case: Survey of generative AI tools such as ChatGPT and Claude used as coding assistants, feedback providers, and conversational tutors in computer science education; includes RAG-enhanced chat-based support for context-aware tutoring.
AI-driven grading and feedback for programming/code tasks, including real-time formative feedback, correctness checking, and automated evaluation of student code and AI-generated submissions.

finding.finding_summary: This review finds that generative AI can improve efficiency and support creative coding work in computer science education, but accuracy problems such as hallucinations and error propagation can undermine learning and task correctness. The paper synthesizes prior studies rather than reporting a new experiment, so no pooled effect size is reported; reported concerns include hallucinations accounting for 53% of errors in one cited study (Wu et al.).
finding.measure: Accuracy, correctness, and reliability of AI-generated educational/code outputs; hallucination and error propagation rates in cited literature
finding.study_size: 52 papers reviewed; cited primary studies vary

finding.finding_summary: The review concludes that GenAI tools can streamline grading, provide timely feedback, and reduce educator workload in large classes, especially for routine programming tasks. This is a narrative synthesis of 52 papers, so no aggregate effect size is estimated, but the paper consistently frames efficiency gains as one of the main benefits of AI-supported assessment and feedback.
finding.measure: Grading efficiency, feedback timeliness, and educator workload
finding.study_size: 52 papers reviewed; cited primary studies vary

finding.finding_summary: The review reports that AI assistance may support problem-solving and creative exploration, but over-reliance can blur authorship, weaken independent work, and complicate the development of critical thinking. The paper does not provide new quantitative estimates; its conclusion is based on synthesis of prior literature and repeatedly calls for AI literacy and human oversight to protect these skills.
finding.measure: Critical thinking, problem-solving, creativity, and authenticity of student work
finding.study_size: 52 papers reviewed; cited primary studies vary

finding.finding_summary: The paper argues that AI integration creates substantial institutional challenges around academic integrity, assessment policy, bias mitigation, and the need for human-AI hybrid evaluation models. It recommends clear guidelines, AI literacy, and institutional governance changes, but reports no new causal evidence or effect size because it is a review article.
finding.measure: Academic integrity, assessment policy, bias detection/mitigation, and governance frameworks
finding.study_size: 52 papers reviewed; cited primary studies vary
